title: add safe egress guardrail and peered controlplane authz mapper
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: customers running Private deployments requested clearer guardrails for control-plane egress and a safer, auditable way to automate cross-account peering authorization for control-plane endpoints. This PR adds a reusable egress profile/guardrail that enforces explicit prefix-lists and NAT/external-proxy rules during control-plane provisioning, plus a pluggable 'authz-mapper' that signs and validates peering authorization tokens when creating cross-account VPC peering and privatelink endpoints. Changes are intended to minimize blast radius during upgrades and to make terraform plans idempotent across accounts. What this PR does: 1) terraform/modules/controlplane: new module controlplane-egress-profile.tf + prefixlist templates and validation; 2) terraform/modules/peering: add authz_mapper integration with signed token flow and conditional IAM role bindings for peering accept; 3) helm/controlplane: values and chart helpers to surface egressProfile and authzMapper config for Private deployments; 4) installer/pkg/peering: new authz_mapper.go (sign/verify) and small helper to annotate peering resources with signed metadata; 5) installer/upgrade: include a preflight that validates egress prefix-lists and fails fast with clear remediation steps; 6) tests/integration: add an end-to-end smoke that simulates cross-account peering with signed token exchange. Backwards compatibility: the authz mapper is opt-in via a boolean flag and a signing key secret; if disabled, existing peering behavior is preserved. Rollout plan: merge to main behind a feature flag, run a staged rollout to internal staging accounts, then enable for customers via configuration and announce in release notes. Rollback plan: disable the feature flag and revert the small installer binary (two-line config) - terraform modules are additive and safe to keep; where necessary, we provide a migration script that removes signed annotations from existing peering resources. Security considerations: signing keys are stored in KMS-backed secrets; we added explicit guidance for rotating keys and an emergency revoke procedure. Related: ENG-2451, small follow-up will add CloudTrail-based alerting for mismatched signatures. Docs: included README snippets and helm values docs for customers.
